meta.titre: Energy conversions: conservation, kinetic energy and efficiency

sections.contenu_markdown: The Sanaga river drops over a long height at Edea and Song Loulou, and the falling water turns turbines that light up Douala and Yaoundé. When you switch on a torch, chemical energy in the cells becomes light, and when you charge a phone on a solar panel in Maroua, light becomes electrical energy. Energy never appears from nothing and never disappears: it only changes form. The GCE asks you to state this law, to name the energy change in common devices, and to calculate potential energy, kinetic energy and efficiency.

items: Energy is measured in joules (J) and power in watts (W), where $1\ \mathrm{W} = 1\ \mathrm{J\,s^{-1}}$.
Gravitational potential energy depends on mass, height and $g = 10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$; kinetic energy depends on mass and speed.
Energy exists in many forms: kinetic, potential, chemical, electrical, heat, light, sound, nuclear.

sections.titre: Conservation of energy, energy changes and efficiency
sections.contenu_markdown:
**Law of conservation of energy.** Energy cannot be created or destroyed. It can only be changed from one form to another, so the total energy of an isolated system stays the same.

**Useful formulae.**

- Gravitational potential energy: $E_p = mgh$ (with $m$ in kg, $h$ in m, $g = 10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$).
- Kinetic energy: $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$.
- Work done by a force along its direction: $W = F \times d$, measured in joules; work done is the energy transferred.
- Efficiency $= \dfrac{\text{useful energy output}}{\text{total energy input}} \times 100\%$. It can never exceed $100\%$, because some energy is always wasted, mostly as heat.

**Common energy changes.**

| Device or process | Energy change |
|---|---|
| Loudspeaker | electrical $\to$ sound |
| Dynamo or generator | kinetic $\to$ electrical |
| Electric motor | electrical $\to$ kinetic |
| Solar cell | light $\to$ electrical |
| Filament lamp | electrical $\to$ light and heat |
| Burning charcoal | chemical $\to$ heat and light |
| Battery | chemical $\to$ electrical |
| Hydroelectric station | gravitational potential $\to$ kinetic (water and turbine) $\to$ electrical |

When a falling body loses height, it loses potential energy and gains the same amount of kinetic energy, provided air resistance is ignored. When it lands, its kinetic energy becomes heat and sound in the ground and the object.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When an object is dropped, thrown up, or slides down a smooth slope and you must find a height or a speed.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Write $E_p$ lost $= E_k$ gained, that is $mgh = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$. The mass cancels, so $v = \sqrt{2gh}$ for a body dropped from rest. For an object thrown upwards, its starting kinetic energy equals the potential energy at the highest point, so $h = \dfrac{v^2}{2g}$.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a machine or appliance gives out less useful energy than it takes in.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Wasted energy $=$ energy input $-$ useful energy output. In a lamp, the useful output is light and the wasted part is heat. In an engine, friction turns part of the chemical energy into heat in the moving parts. Efficiency can also be found from power: $\text{efficiency} = \dfrac{\text{useful power output}}{\text{power input}} \times 100\%$.

sections.enonce_markdown: A coconut of mass $4\ \mathrm{kg}$ falls from a palm tree. It starts from rest at a height of $20\ \mathrm{m}$ above the ground. Ignore air resistance and take $g = 10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. Find (a) its potential energy at the top, (b) its kinetic energy just before it hits the ground, (c) its speed at that instant, and say what happens to the energy when it lands.

etapes.action: Write the formula for potential energy and substitute.
etapes.justification: Potential energy depends on mass, $g$ and height above the ground.

etapes.action: Use conservation of energy to find the kinetic energy at the ground.
etapes.justification: With no air resistance, all the potential energy lost becomes kinetic energy.

etapes.action: Write the kinetic energy formula and solve for $v$.
etapes.justification: We know $E_k$ and the mass, so we can find the speed.

etapes.action: Say where the energy goes on landing.
etapes.justification: The coconut stops, so its kinetic energy cannot remain; energy is conserved, so it changes form.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The $800\ \mathrm{J}$ becomes heat and sound in the ground and the coconut.

sections.conclusion_markdown: The potential energy is $800\ \mathrm{J}$, the kinetic energy at the ground is $800\ \mathrm{J}$ and the speed is $20\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. On landing, the kinetic energy is changed to heat and sound.

items.erreur_markdown: "The torch battery uses up its energy, so the energy is destroyed."
items.pourquoi_faux: Energy is never destroyed. The chemical energy of the cell is changed to light and heat.
items.correction_markdown: Write the energy change: chemical $\to$ electrical $\to$ light and heat. The total is conserved.

items.pourquoi_faux: This inverts the ratio and gives a value above $100\%$. A real machine always wastes some energy.
items.correction_markdown: Use $\dfrac{\text{useful output}}{\text{total input}} \times 100\%$, which is always below $100\%$.

items.pourquoi_faux: The formula needs the mass in kilograms. Using grams gives a value 1000 times too large.

items.erreur_markdown: "$E_k = mv^2$ for a $2\ \mathrm{kg}$ ball at $3\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ gives $18\ \mathrm{J}$."
items.pourquoi_faux: The formula has a factor $\frac{1}{2}$. The speed is squared, but the half is part of the definition.

items.erreur_markdown: "A loudspeaker changes sound into electrical energy."
items.pourquoi_faux: This reverses the change. A loudspeaker receives electrical energy and gives out sound.
items.correction_markdown: Loudspeaker: electrical $\to$ sound. Microphone: sound $\to$ electrical.

items.enonce_markdown: A lamp takes in $200\ \mathrm{J}$ of electrical energy and gives out $30\ \mathrm{J}$ of light. Find (a) the energy wasted and its form, and (b) the efficiency of the lamp.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Wasted energy $= 200 - 30 = 170\ \mathrm{J}$, given out as **heat**.

(b) Efficiency $= \dfrac{30}{200} \times 100\% = \mathbf{15\%}$.

items.enonce_markdown: A ball of mass $0.5\ \mathrm{kg}$ is thrown vertically upwards with an initial speed of $12\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Ignoring air resistance and taking $g = 10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$, calculate (a) its initial kinetic energy and (b) the greatest height it reaches.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.5 \times 12^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.5 \times 144 = \mathbf{36\ J}$.

(b) At the highest point all of the kinetic energy has become potential energy: $mgh = 36$, so $h = \dfrac{36}{0.5 \times 10} = \dfrac{36}{5} = \mathbf{7.2\ m}$.

items.enonce_markdown: A small hydroelectric plant receives $800\ \mathrm{kg}$ of water every second from a reservoir whose water falls through a height of $25\ \mathrm{m}$. The overall efficiency of the plant is $60\%$. Take $g = 10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. Find (a) the potential energy given up by the water each second, (b) the electrical power produced, and (c) the number of $100\ \mathrm{W}$ bulbs this power can light. State the energy chain in the plant.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) $E_p = mgh = 800 \times 10 \times 25 = 200\,000\ \mathrm{J}$ each second, so the input power is $200\,000\ \mathrm{W}$ ($200\ \mathrm{kW}$).

(b) Electrical power $= 60\% \times 200\,000 = \mathbf{120\,000\ W}$ ($120\ \mathrm{kW}$).

(c) Number of bulbs $= \dfrac{120\,000}{100} = \mathbf{1\,200}$ bulbs.

Energy chain: gravitational potential energy of the water $\to$ kinetic energy of the water and turbine $\to$ electrical energy in the generator, with some energy wasted as heat and sound.

items_markdown: Energy is never created or destroyed; it is changed from one form to another and the total stays constant.
$E_p = mgh$ and $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$, with mass in kilograms and $g = 10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.
A falling object turns potential energy into kinetic energy; on landing the kinetic energy becomes heat and sound.
Efficiency $= \dfrac{\text{useful output}}{\text{total input}} \times 100\%$ and is always less than $100\%$.
Know the energy change of a device in the right direction, for example a microphone is sound to electrical and a loudspeaker is electrical to sound.
